pages.title: Tours
pages.content:
Tours

Five guided coast tours from three to seven days, each with its distance, climbing and grade.

pages.title: The Harbour Line
pages.content:
The Harbour Line

Three gentle days, 142 km and 1,180 m of climbing, Grade 1 Easy, from €690 per person in a twin room.

pages.title: Grades & Fitness
pages.content:
Grades & fitness

Four riding grades, from Grade 1 Easy at 40–50 km a day to Grade 4 Strong at 65–80 km a day.

pages.title: Bike Hire
pages.content:
Bike hire

Road or hybrid bike, helmet, two panniers, bottle cages and repair kit, fitted by our mechanic in Saltmere.

pages.title: Luggage & Van
pages.content:
Luggage & van

One bag of up to 20 kg per guest travels ahead in the support van and is in your room by 15:00.

pages.title: Departures & Prices

Departures & prices

Departures run from April to October. Prices are per person in a twin room, with a 20% deposit to hold your place.

posts.title: The day the wind turned at the lighthouse
posts.excerpt: Tomas Reyes on a Lighthouse Loop morning when a flat headland road became a headwind, and how the group rode it together.
posts.content:
Tomas Reyes leads the Lighthouse Loop most weeks between April and October. On the third morning the headland road is usually the easy part of the day. This September the wind turned a quarter past ten, and the flat road became a long, patient climb into the grass.

We shortened the gaps, put the two strongest riders at the front in turns and kept the pace at the low end of Grade 2. Nobody was left behind and the van was waiting at the lighthouse car park with tea at noon, exactly as planned.

The lesson is an old one on this coast: the wind sets the pace, not the clock. That is why every departure has two guides and a van driver, and why we never promise a speed.

posts.title: Fixing a puncture in ninety seconds
posts.excerpt: Lena Vos, our mechanic, shows how a roadside puncture is mended in ninety seconds with the kit that comes with every hire bike.
posts.content:
Lena Vos runs the Saltmere workshop and fits every hire bike. Her roadside puncture routine takes about ninety seconds once the wheel is off: lever, check the tyre, new tube, a few strokes of the pump, wheel back on.

Every hire bike leaves the workshop with a repair kit, a spare tube and a mini pump. The guides carry more, and the van carries two spare bikes, but a quick fix at the roadside keeps the whole group moving.

If you would like to practise before your departure, ask Lena at the bike fitting. She is happy to hand you the tyre levers.

posts.title: Bags on the quay before we arrive
posts.excerpt: Samuel Okafor drives the van on every departure and explains how your bag reaches the next harbour before you do.
posts.content:
Samuel Okafor has driven the support van on every departure since 2016. Bags go onto the van at 08:30 each morning, one bag of up to 20 kg per guest, and by 15:00 they are standing in the hall of the next guesthouse.

He takes the coast road a little faster than the riders, stops at the harbour café to check the lunch booking and is usually on the quay with the kettle when the first bike rolls in.

It is a small thing, but it changes the day: you ride with a day bag and a clear head, and your clean clothes are already waiting.
